recommendations.recommendation: Use slim Python 3.12 base images, multi-stage builds, and `.dockerignore` to keep images small and layer-friendly.
Pin CPU/memory limits per container and run as non-root with a HEALTHCHECK so scheduler placement is predictable.
Right-size named volumes, prune orphaned volumes, and move cold artifacts to MinIO object storage.
Enable Redis eviction policies, cap cache keys, and use lazy initialization so Redis failures degrade gracefully.
Add matching indexes, bound connection pools, and use `autovacuum` tuning before adding hardware.
Bound queue lengths, set TTLs on dead-letter queues, and enforce consumer prefetch limits.
Apply lifecycle policies to archive old objects and enable compression for cold buckets.
Size worker concurrency to the queue depth instead of the host core count; pause idle workers.
Schedule heavy background jobs off-peak and use the bounded queue instead of unbounded fan-out.
Prefer self-hosted free-first components, prune unused resources, and right-size before scaling out.
